correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=2 the four exhaustive kinds of geodesic triples give iff conditions on upper/lower rail-edge index sets and allowed rungs. The seven horizontal-cardinality categories form a disjoint partition and yield the exact face polynomial. Exhaustively analyzing all admissible horizontal profiles under single-edge augmentations yields four disjoint facet families and the exact facet polynomial. Boundary n=2 and all stated binomial conventions are checked. A standalone BFS shortest-path enumerator (not using the formulas to generate obstructions) exhaustively verifies all 2^(3n-2) subsets for n=2..7, compares every coefficient, and tests extensions and all forbidden triples; symbolic independent structural tests cover n=8..40. Finite tests are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Geodesic exclusion on the natural open-ladder family is a studied extremal problem. The exact face polynomial gives all configuration counts, while the full facet polynomial reveals every possible inclusion-maximal size from three through n+2 and explains nonpurity with unbounded facet-size spread. These are intrinsically motivated complex-level invariants and not routine renamings of the previously known maximum count. The proof provides an exhaustive structural classification, not just isolated small-n computations.
